domain_restrictions: x ranges over all real numbers
P is a predicate defined on integers (so P(z) and P(z - 1) are well-formed)
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: If f maps real numbers to some codomain and satisfies f(x + 1) = f(x) for all real x, and if there exists an integer z such that P(z) holds, then P(z - 1) holds for that same integer z.

variables.name: x
variables.role: dummy variable used in the period condition

variables.name: z
variables.role: existential witness for which P(z) holds

witness_dependencies: the conclusion P(z - 1) depends on the particular integer z that witnesses the assumption P(z)

statement_nl: Assume that for every real number x, f(x + 1) = f(x), and assume P(z) for some integer z. Then P(z - 1).
